title: Why I Stopped Multitasking
topic: ความคิดเห็น/ประสบการณ์
lines: For years I was proud of being a multitasker. I answered emails during
meetings, listened to podcasts while studying, and kept ten browser tabs
open at all times. I believed **this** made me efficient. Then I read about
a study from Stanford University that changed my mind.
Researchers compared heavy multitaskers with people who usually did one
thing at a time. To their surprise, the heavy multitaskers performed
worse on almost every test of attention and memory. **They** were more easily
distracted and slower at switching between tasks, the very skill they
I decided to try an experiment of my own. For one month, I did only one
task at a time. I turned off notifications and checked my messages just
three times a day. The first week was difficult; I kept reaching for my
phone without thinking. But by the end of the month, I was finishing my
work faster and, more importantly, I felt calmer. **Those** around me noticed
too. My sister said I finally listened when she talked. I still slip back
into old habits sometimes, but now I know what my attention is worth.
